What disqualifies a protein bar from being gluten free

We check the Gluten Free (Y/N) label on file for every bar, then cross-check ingredient lists ourselves for wheat and barley or malt, the two gluten sources that show up by name in our data. 785 of 1,245 bars, about 63%, carry a gluten free label. The other 460, about 37%, don't.

Wheat is the most common named culprit at 62 bars (5.0% of the full database), followed by barley or malt at 28 bars (2.2%). The remaining 388 bars, 31.2% of the full database, show no wheat or barley in their own ingredient list at all. They just aren't labeled gluten free, which is a different claim from actually containing gluten.

Wheat
62 bars5.0%
The most common named gluten source, usually as wheat flour, a wheat-based crisp, or a graham/cookie piece mixed into the bar.
Found in: Anabar, Barebells, Built, CLIF Bar
and 12 moreHide, Einstein, FITCRUNCH, Fields Good, Gatorade, Lenny & Larry's, Met-RX, MyProtein, Nature Valley, Neoh, NuGo, Power Crunch, Wonderslim
Barley / Malt
28 bars2.2%
Shows up as barley malt extract or malt syrup, usually a flavoring or sweetener rather than a structural ingredient.
Found in: Built, CLIF Bar, Fields Good, Power Crunch
and 1 moreHide, Wonderslim
Not labeled gluten free
388 bars31.2%
No wheat or barley shows up anywhere in the ingredient list we can find, but the brand hasn't labeled or certified the bar gluten free either. That is a labeling gap, not proof the bar contains gluten.

What we found screening 1,245 bars

31.2%
of all protein bars show no wheat or barley, yet still aren't labeled gluten free
388 of the 1,245 bars we track have no wheat or barley anywhere in their own ingredient list, but the brand hasn't labeled or certified them gluten free. Not being labeled gluten free is not the same as containing gluten.
Wheat is the clearest single gluten source.
62 bars (5.0% of the database) name wheat directly, more than double the barley/malt count.
CLIF Bar shows the pattern clearly.
5 of CLIF Bar's 14 flavors use wheat directly. None of CLIF Bar's flavors are labeled gluten free.
106 brands are gluten free across their entire lineup.
Led by Larabar (29), think! (22), Bobo's (21), Aloha (18), these brands never reach for wheat or barley in the first place, rather than swapping it out flavor by flavor.
Gluten free bars grade slightly better than the database average.
58.9% of gluten free bars grade A or B, against 55.3% database-wide.
Gluten free bars average less protein, about the same fiber.
Gluten free bars average 12.1g of protein against a database-wide average of 13.3g, but carry about the same fiber (5.0g vs. 4.9g).
NuGo splits closer to even than any other brand.
23 of NuGo's 30 flavors are gluten free, the rest are not. It is the largest genuinely mixed lineup in the database.

This guide covers gluten free bars specifically. The Bar Finder covers all 1,000+ bars in the database, and you set the filters: protein, sugar, fiber, calories, ingredient grade, brand, certifications, and specific ingredients to exclude. No sponsored picks, no subjective taste tests. You decide what matters.

How we score →
  • Every ingredient is scored individually against a canonical database, not just flagged good or bad
  • Position in the ingredient list matters, earlier ingredients carry more weight
  • Each bar's total becomes a single letter grade, A through F

Frequently asked questions

We use the Gluten Free (Y/N) label on file for each bar. 785 of the 1,245 bars we track carry that label. We also cross-check ingredient lists ourselves for wheat and barley or malt, the two named gluten sources that show up most in the data.
785 of the 1,245 bars we track are labeled gluten free, spanning 122 brands. 152 of those 785 bars grade A for ingredient quality.
No. 5 of CLIF Bar's 14 flavors use wheat directly, and none of CLIF Bar's flavors carry a gluten free label.
Yes. All 29 Larabar flavors we track are labeled gluten free. Larabar builds its bars around dates, nuts, and fruit rather than a wheat-based binder or crisp.
Wheat. It shows up by name in 62 of the 1,245 bars we track, more than double the count for barley or malt. Most other non-gluten-free bars simply aren't labeled, without a named gluten ingredient we can find.
Not necessarily. 388 of the 460 bars that don't carry our gluten free label show no wheat or barley anywhere in their own ingredient list. The brand just hasn't labeled or certified the bar, which is a different claim from it containing gluten.
Yes. NuGo splits closest to even of any brand we checked: 23 of 30 flavors are gluten free. Always check the specific flavor, not just the brand.
785 bars across 122 brands carry a gluten free label, led by brands like Larabar and think! that qualify across their entire lineup. The full ranked list is in the table below, sorted by ingredient quality.
460 of the 1,245 bars we track don't carry a gluten free label. Wheat is the most common named reason, followed by barley or malt. Most of the remaining bars simply haven't been labeled, without an identifiable gluten ingredient in the list.
No. Gluten free bars in our database grade A or B at a slightly higher rate than the database as a whole (58.9% vs. 55.3%). What they give up on average is protein: gluten free bars average 12.1g against a database-wide average of 13.3g.
We update the database whenever new bars are added or a brand reformulates. Manufacturers do change their ingredient lists over time, so always confirm against the packaging in front of you. This page reflects the database as of 2026-08-26.
